display.purpose: The THE / STORY DESK wordmark only; scaled 16 / 18 / 34 / 58px by placement, tracking ~0.18em of size.

headline.purpose: The <Title> component (paperTypography.title): card and page titles typed on paper, often in capitals.

title.purpose: The <Heading> component (paperTypography.heading): card headings and sheet titles on paper.

body.purpose: All prose typed on paper; loglines in italic.

typed-field.purpose: Text typed into a field on paper: Courier Prime at the chrome body size (16/23).

caption.purpose: Secondary typed lines on paper. Tiers within it are split by type style or size (the beat position line is italic in pencil under a faded-ink definition), never by ink alone: pencil and faded ink are about 1.27:1 apart.

label.purpose: The <Eyebrow> component: typed field headings that label the value beneath them, or head a section inside a card. Never above a heading.

hand-label.purpose: Caveat on masking tape: section labels on the board.

hand-note.purpose: Caveat asides, print captions and the motto. Never data.

chrome-body.purpose: Desk text, button labels and desk fields.

shadows.name: paper-lift
shadows.purpose: Every pinned card, blank slip, print, sticky note and the walnut frame on the desk (native: black 0.45, radius 7, y 3; Android elevation 5).

shadows.name: tag-lift

shadows.name: clip

narrative.overview:
The app is a real room, not an interface in the shape of one. A warm near-black desk sits under a single lamp; above it hangs a cork board in a walnut frame. Every screen is that board: aged index cards typed in Courier Prime, pinned with red and brass push pins, joined by one red string that is both the story's causal chain and the way you move through the app. Section labels are strips of masking tape written on in marker. Characters and scenes are noir prints with handwritten captions. Nothing on the board is a flat UI card; everything is a physical object with a fastening, a slight hand-pinned tilt, and a lamp shadow under it.

The system runs on two surfaces, not two themes. The desk carries chrome in chalk on warm charcoal and the platform face (native headers, controls, the composer). Paper carries everything the story is made of, in ink and type. Components read which surface they sit on, so the same Caption is chalk on the desk and ink on a card, and a color chosen at screen scope is carried to its paper counterpart when drawn on a card. Density is that of a working board: many cards, tight typed groups inside each card, generous cork between them.

The world refuses the category default of flat cards in a tab app: navigation is a string you follow, sections are tape, status is a rubber stamp, discoveries are sticky notes. Photographs are generated and illustrative and say so in `assets/story/PROVENANCE.md`.
keyCharacteristics: Two surfaces with paired palettes: chalk on the desk, ink on paper.
One interactive accent, brass; red belongs to the string, the pins and failure.
Courier Prime for everything typed on paper, Caveat for tape and margins, Cinzel for the wordmark alone, the platform face for chrome.
Physical depth: paper lifts off cork under one overhead lamp.
Paper is cut, not rounded; cards hang with a small deterministic tilt.
The red string connects cards in reading order and carries navigation.

rules.name: The Two Surfaces Rule
rules.body: Every color is a role on a surface. Each desk role has a paper counterpart with the same key, and a color handed from the desk to a card resolves to its paper counterpart. Never add a role to one surface only.

rules.name: The Brass Hand Rule
rules.body: Brass is the only interactive fill and focus color on the desk, and ink is the only interactive fill on paper. String red is never a button, link or focus color. It marks 'you are here' only as material: the red pin on the active nav tag and on the chosen discoveries tab, and the String Highlight edge on the Home filmstrip's current frame. (The direction contract named string red as the accent; the build gave interaction to brass and kept red as material. The build is the record.)

rules.name: The Faded Dye Rule
rules.body: Note dyes are faded, never neon. A sticky note lays its dye over paper fibre at 70%. The discovery filter tags use the same four dyes as flat fills. Stamp ink is the exception: pressed, not faded, at full opacity (see Rubber Stamps).

rules.name: The Typed Paper Rule
rules.body: Anything written onto paper is Courier Prime. Desk chrome (headers, controls, fields, chips, nav labels) is the platform face. Courier Prime appears on the desk only as typed story identity: the hero line, the sidebar project name, panel titles and filmstrip frame labels. Custom faces carry weight in the family name: emphasis on paper swaps to Courier Prime Bold, never a synthesized weight.

rules.name: The Field Label Rule
rules.body: Small tracked capitals are the typed field headings of an index card or title page (PREMISE, THEME STATEMENT, WHOSE MOVE): each labels the value directly beneath it, or heads a section inside a card whose rows follow. A label never sits above a Title or Headline; a heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Hand Is Annotation Rule
rules.body: Caveat labels, captions and asides only. Data, values and anything a user must read precisely are typed.

rules.name: The Nameplate Rule
rules.body: Cinzel appears only in the wordmark.

rules.name: The Reading Order Rule
rules.body: The string joins cards in the order they are read. Stacked cards pin top-left and the thread hangs in the cork gutter to their left, clear of the cards; cards in a row pin at top centre and the thread sags between them.

rules.name: The Lamp Falloff Rule
rules.body: Light pools in the middle of the board and darkens toward the frame. The cork and its raster vignette are one fixed layer under the scrolling cards, so the falloff stays with the viewport and shades the cork, never the paper: text on paper keeps its contrast into the corners.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Every lift shadow falls downward with a soft blur in black (rgba(0,0,0,…)). The warm tints belong to the string shadow and the chalk halo. The string alone casts a hard offset stroke shadow (1.5px right, 3px down), because string lies on the board. No other zero-blur, sideways or colored shadows; the only glow is the bead riding the string.

rules.name: The Cut Paper Rule
rules.body: Paper takes 2px corners at most and hangs by a pin, a strip of tape, or nothing. Rounded rectangles and pills never stand in for paper.

dos: Do put every piece of content on the board on paper: an index card, slip, print, sticky note or stamp, fastened by pin, tape or nothing.
Do read the surface: chalk and the platform face for desk chrome (#14110E), ink and Courier Prime on paper (#EDE3CC).
Do keep brass (#C9A25B) as the only interactive accent on the desk and ink (#2B241C) as the interactive fill on paper.
Do join related cards with the red string in reading order, and let navigation travel along it.
Do give every outcome tier and canon status its word on a stamp as well as its color.
Do keep touch targets at 44pt, extending small controls with hit slop.
Do tilt pinned cards deterministically by key (up to ±0.8°) and hang forms and long reading square.
donts: Don't use string red (#A8201A) for buttons, links or focus; it belongs to the string, the pins (including the pin that marks the current place) and failure.
Don't round paper past 2px, and don't use a pill as a piece of paper; pills belong only to small controls (chips, icon buttons, reaction counters), on the desk or on a card.
Don't set data or values in Caveat, or use Cinzel anywhere but the wordmark.
Don't set a tracked-capitals label above a heading; labels head values and in-card sections only.
Don't add zero-blur, sideways or colored shadows beyond the string's own stroke shadow and the bead's glow; depth comes from the one lamp overhead.
Don't use flat bordered UI cards on the cork, or textures that are not from the desk's own materials (cork, walnut, paper, tape).

Don't type text on paper lighter than pencil (#5B4F40), the lightest paper ink: it holds 5.5:1 on slip paper (#E2D5B8) and 6.2:1 on aged ivory (#EDE3CC). The lighter canon hues (#554A3C, #6A5D4C) reach paper only pressed into a stamp.

Don't mark where the next item goes with a dashed or dotted outline or an empty drop zone; it is a blank slip lying loose on the cork, or bare cork with a handwritten note. (The desk Badge's dashed and dotted outlines are canon status marks for proposed and unknown, not placeholders.)
